follow-up time: Until April 2016 (mean of 3.35 years after treatment for those who had a pregnancy leading to delivery)
exposure: excisional treatment for high-grade cervical intra-epithelial neoplasia (CIN2+)
large loop excision of the transformation zone
cohort: 2316 women aged 25-45 years who underwent excisional treatment for CIN2+ at two hospitals in Italy between 2005-2014, and 57,937 untreated women of the same age, from the same centers
finding: Cervical excisional treatment was associated with an increased risk of preterm delivery, PROM, and dystocic births, but a lower risk of cesarean section.
mod_finding: Techniques removing or ablating more tissue, such as large loop excision of the transformation zone, were associated with worse obstetric outcomes.
